claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about your child or children. 

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?**

The age determines which rules apply. Please let me know:
- The name(s) of your child/children
- Their age(s)

This will help me check which category they fall into:
- **Under 16** - Generally automatically qualify
- **16 to 19** - Need to be in education or training
- **20 or over** - Generally not eligible

Once I know their ages, I can continue with the eligibility check.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 6 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thanks for that information! That's helpful context. So you're claiming for **Alex, who is 6 years old** and lives with you at home.

Since Alex is under 16, let me navigate to the next step of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is 6 years old (under 16), we're moving forward in the assessment. 

Now I need to check: **Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

For a 6-year-old, the answer is almost certainly no - he wouldn't typically be in paid employment. So the answer should be **yes** - he's working less than 24 hours per week (or not working at all).

Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he's not working at all. He's only 6, so he's just at primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected for a 6-year-old. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check: **Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

For a 6-year-old, this would be highly unusual, but I need to confirm - is Alex receiving any of these benefits in his own name?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a young child, so nothing like that applies to him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I'd expect. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check on apprenticeships. At 6 years old, Alex definitely won't be in an apprenticeship, so this is straightforward:

**Is Alex NOT in an apprenticeship?**

Given his age, the answer should be **yes** - he's not in any apprenticeship. Let me confirm that's correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - he's definitely not in an apprenticeship. He's only 6, so he's just at primary school like I mentioned.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me move forward to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. This is important for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you (the claimant) meet UK residency requirements?**

There are several paths that could qualify you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the main path for most people
2. **You have settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. **You have pre-settled status** and are working, seeking work, have sufficient resources, or are a student
4. **You're a Crown servant** living abroad in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to your situation? To keep things simple - do you normally live in the UK? If yes, then you'd qualify under the first path.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm based here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward then. You meet the residency requirements by normally living in the UK. Let me continue to the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check: **Are you responsible for Alex?**

You mentioned that Alex lives with you at home, so this should be straightforward. Responsibility means either:

1. **You live with the child** - Which you do with Alex
2. **You contribute to the child's upkeep** - Through food, clothes, housing, etc.
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Since you've already said Alex lives with you at home, you clearly meet this requirement. Can you confirm that Alex lives with you and you're responsible for his care and upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives with me and I look after him. I provide everything he needs - food, clothes, housing, all of that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you're definitely responsible for Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check: **Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or could anyone else potentially claim?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent also claiming for him?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent or other family member) claiming for him?
- Are you and another person in dispute about who should claim?

Or is it just you claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's just me claiming for him. Nobody else is getting Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's current living situation:

**Is Alex currently:**
- In hospital?
- In care (local authority care)?
- Fostered?
- Living normally at home with you (the standard situation)?

You mentioned he lives at home with you, so I believe the answer is that he's living normally. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he's living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, not in care, and not fostered. Just living at home like a normal 6-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the standard situation. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! We're almost at the final check. 

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words - is the council NOT financially supporting his housing or care? For a child living at home with you, the answer should be **yes** - the council isn't paying for these things.

Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - the council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance. I'm supporting him myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final check complete. Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me provide you with your final eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Good News - You're ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!

**For: Alex (age 6)**

### Your Eligibility Summary:

You **ARE eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex. He meets all the required criteria:

✅ **Qualifying child** - Alex is 6 years old (under 16)  
✅ **Not working full-time** - He's at primary school, not in paid work  
✅ **Not receiving disqualifying benefits** - No ESA or UC in his own right  
✅ **Not in disqualifying apprenticeship** - Not applicable at his age  
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You live in the UK  
✅ **You're responsible for him** - You live with Alex and provide his food, clothes, and housing  
✅ **You're the only claimant** - No one else is claiming for him  
✅ **Normal living arrangements** - He's at home with you, not in hospital, care, or foster arrangements  
✅ **Council not funding his care** - You're supporting him yourself  

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, there may be a tax charge
5. **Payment frequency** - Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly in certain circumstances)

For more information and to make your claim, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

You are the only person claiming Child Benefit for him. Alex lives normally at home with you and is not in hospital, care, or foster arrangements. The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance. Alex therefore meets all eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.
